custom_logic_notes: Channel EA uses a Donchian-style price channel (highest high / lowest low over N periods) to define breakout levels. When price breaks above the upper channel, a buy stop order is placed at the upper channel level; when price breaks below the lower channel, a sell stop is placed at the lower channel level. The trailing stop dynamically follows the channel boundary - for longs it trails to the lower channel, for shorts it trails to the upper channel. Stop levels are recalculated every new bar. The EA modifies existing position SL to match the evolving channel boundary, creating a channel-based trailing stop system. Pending orders are deleted and replaced when channel boundaries shift.
python_conversion_notes: This EA requires tick-level backtesting for accuracy because it places pending stop orders at channel boundaries and modifies SL on every new bar based on recalculated channel levels. The channel calculation itself is simple (rolling max high / min low), but the order management is complex: placing, deleting, and replacing stop orders as channel boundaries shift, and modifying position SL to trail the channel. The pending order lifecycle management (create, check if still valid, delete if channel shifts, replace at new level) is the hardest part to replicate in Python. Must implement a full pending order state machine and bar-by-bar channel recalculation with intrabar tick simulation for stop order fills.
